context: Session TTL boundary and an interval sweeper, where the code under test reads Date.now() directly and schedules with setInterval. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reaches the boundary by arithmetic on lastSeenAt (setting it to now minus TTL) rather than by controlling the clock, or hand-patches Date.now with a jest.fn and never restores it. Both leave the sweeper untestable, because setInterval still runs on real time. The skill's value is a single mechanism - a faked system clock - that covers Date and timers together.

checklist.name: Test file created
checklist.description: A file src/session.test.js exists and contains at least one test.

checklist.name: System time is set deterministically
checklist.description: The test fixes the clock with jest.setSystemTime() (or useFakeTimers with a now/doNotFake configuration that pins Date) so Date.now() inside session.js returns a known value. Reaching the boundary only by back-dating lastSeenAt while Date.now() still returns real time scores at most half, because it leaves the sweeper uncontrollable.

checklist.name: Boundary tested on both sides
checklist.description: There is an assertion at TTL minus one millisecond returning not-expired AND an assertion at exactly TTL returning expired. Testing only one side, or only a comfortably-past value, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Sweeper driven by advancing the clock
checklist.description: A test starts the sweeper, advances time across at least one sweep interval, and asserts expired entries were removed from the store while live entries remain. A test that calls the sweep logic directly without ever letting the interval fire scores at most half.

checklist.name: Activity refreshes the deadline
checklist.description: A test touches a session partway through the window, advances past the original deadline, and asserts the session is still valid.

checklist.name: Global Date is not hand-patched
checklist.description: MUST NOT. The test does not reassign or monkey-patch the global clock by hand - no `Date.now = jest.fn()`, no `global.Date = class ...`, no jest.spyOn(Date, 'now') left as the sole mechanism. These bypass the timer system so setInterval is unaffected, and they leak if not restored. Any such assignment scores zero on this criterion.

checklist.name: Clock and timers restored
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave a faked clock installed. The file restores real timers after the tests via afterEach(jest.useRealTimers) or equivalent.

checklist.name: No real elapsed time
checklist.description: MUST NOT. No real sleep, no real-delay promise, and no raised test timeout used to wait out the sweep interval.
